questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the core tradeoff between Terraform workspaces and separate state files per environment?
options: There is no real difference between the two approaches
Separate state files cannot be used with shared modules
Workspaces are always the correct choice and separate state files are a deprecated pattern
Workspaces trade isolation for convenience; separate state files trade convenience for isolation
questions.explain: Workspaces are low-overhead but share backend, provider, and credentials; separate directories cost more duplication but give real isolation.

questions.q: Why can't workspaces alone restrict which team or credential is allowed to touch a prod environment?
options: Workspaces automatically assign different Azure RBAC roles to each environment
Terraform Cloud is required before credential separation is possible
Every workspace in a configuration shares the same backend, provider block, and typically the same credentials
Workspace permissions are configured in a separate permissions.tf file
questions.explain: If a credential can reach the shared backend, it can reach every workspace in it — there's no built-in per-workspace permission boundary.

questions.q: In the lesson's directory-per-environment example, what stays identical between envs/dev and envs/prod?
options: The backend.tf file contents
The variable values passed into the module
The storage account used for state
The shared module being called (e.g. module "network" { source = "../../modules/network" })
questions.explain: Each environment directory has its own backend.tf and variable values, but both call the same shared module — the module code is never duplicated.

questions.q: What does giving prod its own backend.tf with a different storage_account_name actually buy you?
options: A separate access policy and Azure RBAC role assignments distinct from dev's backend
A smaller Terraform state file
Automatic Sentinel policy enforcement
Faster terraform apply runs
questions.explain: A different storage account can sit in its own resource group with its own access policy, so dev credentials literally cannot reach prod's state.

questions.q: Per this lesson's guidance, when should separate state files be chosen over workspaces?
options: Only when using AWS instead of Azure
Never — workspaces are always sufficient for any number of environments
When environments need different teams, different approval gates, or genuinely diverging configuration — not just different scale
Whenever there are more than two environments
questions.explain: Workspaces fit environments that are structurally identical and trusted to the same people; separate directories fit environments that need a real boundary.
